To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HIF, an endogenous inhibitor of Na+, K(+)-ATPases with ouabain like properties, constricts pulmonary artery rings from spontaneously hypertensive rats but not from normotensive controls.

the pulmonary hypertension of spontaneously-hypertensive rats (SHR) may be due, at least in part, to an increased sensitivity of the pulmonary arteries to the Na,K-ATPase-inhibiting effect of a hypothalamic factor (HIF).

HIF causes a greater increase in tension in pulmonary artery rings from spontaneously hypertensive rats than from age-matched normo-tensive Sprague-Da-wley rats, and the increase is greater than in aortic rings from spontaneously hyperten-sive rats.

the role of the Na+, K(+)-ATPases in the regulation of vascular tone.
the role of HIF in the pathogenesis and treatment of systemic hypertension.
the role of the Na+, K(+)-ATPases in the regulation of vascular tone and blood pressure.

the pulmonary hypertension of SHRs is associated with an increase in sensitivity of PA to HIF.
HIF is a novel vasoconstrictor of the pulmonary artery of the spontaneously hypertensive rat.

the pulmonary hypertension in SHRs may be caused by a combination of increased sensitivity to HIF, a circulating inhibitor of the Na+, K(+)-ATPases in the vascular smooth muscle, and increased sympathetic tone, which is known to be increased in this model.

HIF is an endogenous inhibitor of the Na+, K(+)-ATPases that has a role in the pathogenesis and maintenance of systemic hypertension.
the HIF-induced pulmonary hypertension of SHR is due to an increase in vascular tone of the pulmonary arteries.

HIF is a potential contributor to the pulmonary hypertension of SHRs.
the HIF is a potent vasoconstrictor in the pulmonary arteries of SHRs and may be a factor in the pathogenesis pulmonary hypertension in this model of genetic hypertension.
